cfg_story: Across the sweep, accuracy rises from {acc_cfg_1} at s = 1 to {acc_cfg_5} at s = 5 and falls back to {acc_cfg_15} at 15; FD is best at s = 2 ({fd_cfg_2}, better than DDPM at 1,000 steps) and worsens beyond it as samples become bolder and more alike: diversity falls at every step up ({div_cfg_1} to {div_cfg_15}), and pixels at full white grow from {white_cfg_1} to {white_cfg_15}, the grey-scale version of over-saturation. At s = 0 (no label at all) only {acc_cfg_0} match the requested class, about chance.
sd_cfg_note: Read across the row: the empty prompt draws an unrelated indoor scene; s = 1 a sunset coast with no clear lighthouse; from s = 2 the lighthouse is there; past 10 the sky turns deep orange and contrast hardens (mean saturation {sat_cfg_1} at s = 1, {sat_cfg_7.5} at 7.5, {sat_cfg_20} at 20). Scales of 1 or less ran one U-Net pass per step ({sec_cfg_1} s per image) against two above 1 ({sec_cfg_7.5} s).
sd_x07_note: None of the four puts the word on the mug: the text lands on a card beside it. At s = 1 the letters are garbled; at 4 and 7.5 the word reads HELLO (with an added exclamation mark at 7.5); at 15 a heart replaces the O. Guidance made the word legible, not correctly placed: binding text to an object is a limit of the CLIP text encoder and the model, which more guidance does not fix.
